intro: Learn how to express your likes and preferences with the verb gustar and indirect object pronouns.
b1.texto:
The verb **gustar** works differently from English: the liked thing is the grammatical subject, and the person liking it is an indirect object pronoun (**me**, **te**, **le**, **nos**, **os**, **les**).

- With a singular noun or an infinitive, use **gusta**: *Me gusta el café*, *Te gusta leer*.
- With a plural noun, use **gustan**: *Me gustan los libros*.

For emphasis, you can add **a mí**, **a ti**, etc.: *A mí me gusta el café*.
b4.texto:
Compare:
- *Me **gusta** el café* (singular subject).
- *Me **gustan** los libros* (plural subject).
b6.pregunta: Which sentence agrees correctly with a plural subject?
b6.o0.refuerzo: Correct: with plural «los libros», the verb must be «gustan».
b6.o1.refuerzo: Incorrect: with a plural subject, you cannot use singular «gusta».
b6.o2.refuerzo: Incorrect: gustar does not translate as «yo gusto».
b7.pregunta: Complete with the indirect pronoun matching «a mí».
b7.o0.refuerzo: Correct: «a mí» always goes with the pronoun «me».
p.me gusta.consejo: Phrase used when the liked thing is singular or an infinitive.
p.me gustan.consejo: Phrase used when the liked things are plural.
p.te gusta.consejo: Second person singular familiar form of gustar.
p.a mí.consejo: Stressed prepositional phrase adding emphasis before me.
p.no.consejo: Negation adverb placed before the pronoun: no me gusta.
p.los libros.consejo: Plural noun: bound printed literary works.
p.también.consejo: Adverb denoting positive agreement or addition.
p.mucho.consejo: Adverb of quantity used to intensify: me gusta mucho.
b2.f1.texto: Yes, I like it a lot.
b5.f0.texto: Many calm readers like hot coffee in the morning.
b5.f1.texto: Lucía really likes old history books.
b5.f2.texto: She spends pleasant hours in the neighbourhood public library.
b5.f3.texto: Pablo doesn't like black tea with lemon.
b5.f4.texto: He prefers to drink mild natural fruit infusions.
b5.f5.texto: The two colleagues share similar tastes in their free time.
b7.frase: A mí también ___ gusta el café.
b8.frase: A mí también me gusta el café.
p.gusta.consejo: Here «gusta» goes with one thing: «me gusta el café». With several things, use «gustan».
p.aventuras.consejo: The v sounds like b: a-ben-TU-ras. «Libros de aventuras» are adventure books.
p.lectores.consejo: From «leer» (to read): «lector», «lectora». The c before t sounds like k.
p.gustan.consejo: Plural form: it agrees with the thing you like. «Me gustan los libros» (the books are pleasing to me).
p.antiguos.consejo: The «u» is pronounced: an-TI-gwos. Singular masculine: «antiguo»; feminine: «antigua».
p.historia.consejo: The h is silent: is-TO-rya. It also means «story»: «una historia».
p.agradables.consejo: One form for masculine and feminine: «agradable». It comes from «agradar» (to please).
p.limón.consejo: Stress on the last syllable, so it has an accent: li-MON. The plural loses it: «limones».
p.tomar.consejo: Very flexible: «tomar café» (drink) or «tomar el autobús» (catch). Here: to drink.
p.infusiones.consejo: Plural of «infusión»: it loses the accent, and the stress moves: in-fu-SYO-nes.
p.suaves.consejo: The «ua» is one syllable, pronounced «wa»: SWA-bes. Singular: «suave».
p.frutas.consejo: «La fruta» is the fruit in general; «las frutas» talks about different kinds.
p.naturales.consejo: One form for masculine and feminine: «natural»; the plural adds -es: «naturales».
p.gustos.consejo: From «gustar». It also means flavor: «un gusto dulce» (a sweet taste).
p.parecidos.consejo: From «parecer» (to seem): the c before i sounds like th: pa-re-THI-dos.
